provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)

issues.text: The over-time dynamics of the experiment (firms observed daily over a long period) are not appropriately handled, making the treatment effects difficult to interpret; the evaluator sees this as the main fault of the paper.
issues.quote: My main fault with the paper is that the over-time dynamics of the experiment are not appropriately handled, which can make it difficult to interpret the effects of the treatment.

issues.text: The panel specification essentially amounts to a two-way fixed effects model, which the evaluator notes has been repeatedly criticized in the recent econometric literature; the evaluator views this as the main methodological criticism and suggests simpler, easier-to-interpret estimates.
issues.quote: the authors' specification, so far as I can tell, boils down to a two-way fixed effects specification that has been repeatedly criticized by authors in recent years

issues.text: The pre-registration is limited: it gives only a rough description of procedures, and the enrolled sample (24,620 firms) fell short of the stated target of more than 25,000 firms, which limits what can be learned from the experiment.
issues.quote: We have a rough though generally accurate description of the experimental procedures and we are told that they intend to do the survey with more than 25,000 firms across 7 treatment arms.

issues.text: The absence of stated priors about effect sizes and of a formal power analysis means the design's power is not well understood, and simulation would be needed to assess it, which the evaluator considers a limitation of the study.
issues.quote: We do not know what if any priors the authors' had about effect sizes, and we lack a good understanding of the power of the design.

issues.text: Without confirmed priors, results risk being read as firmly established rather than partly exploratory, leading to overgeneralization beyond the original context.
issues.quote: This lack of confirmed priors mean we have to be careful when we generalize beyond this study as we run the risk of confirmation bias

issues.text: Some analyses may not be well-powered despite the large overall sample, as subgroup and more specific estimands can carry substantial noise.
issues.quote: that all analyses will be well-powered, as Tom Cuningham noted about the recent Facebook mega-experiment.

issues.text: The analysis does not report simpler baseline specifications (pooled post-treatment comparisons or firm or district fixed effects only), so the reader cannot assess how the extensive fixed effects and the mediator-related specification affect the estimates.
issues.quote: For these reasons, I think the authors should perform a simple pooled analysis as a baseline specification

issues.text: Including day-by-firm fixed effects may induce post-treatment bias, since they may absorb part of the post-treatment mediator, potentially attenuating treatment effects; several results appear surprisingly noisy given the sample size.
issues.quote: Including the fixed effects as such, that is, without a clear causal model, risks inducing post-treatment bias

issues.text: The authors do not model the time dynamics of the treatment effect (e.g., via splines, event-study or multi-period difference-in-differences methods, or parallel-trends checks), which the evaluator thinks are needed to decompose post-treatment variation.
issues.quote: I think the authors should consider models of time.

issues.text: The paper does not clearly specify which comparisons are used to define the estimated average treatment effect; the evaluator suggests clarifying this using a causal-diagram/sequential ignorability framework.
issues.quote: being clear about which particular comparisons are employed would help make it clear exactly what the average treatment effect is.

issues.text: The causal pathway through mediators is not clearly separated from the total effect; the evaluator argues that the mediated effects are most relevant but the design does not isolate direct versus indirect effects.
issues.quote: we are fairly certain that these mediated effects are the most relevant; it would not seem plausible that the treatment would have much of a direct effect on Y apart from the mechanisms

issues.text: The experiment reports no effect on firm-level pollution when appeals are made privately, and the effect on aggregate pollution is unclear despite reductions in violations, so the claimed mechanisms and pollution impacts are not fully established.
issues.quote: while the treatment lowers violations, its impact on aggregate pollution is less clear (table 7), possibly because firms can meet air quality standards but still pollute substantially.

issues.text: External validity is limited because the treatment's effect depends on the policymaker's utility function (China's emphasis on pollution legitimacy), which the experiment cannot vary; the effects may not replicate where policymakers do not prioritize pollution harms.
issues.quote: If we were to implement the Weibo treatment in an institutional framework that did not prioritize pollution harms, we would not necessarily observe such large treatment effects.

issues.text: The ethical and safety implications for citizens posting appeals are not fully addressed; in other authoritarian settings social media activism could invite repression, and the ethics analysis relies on China-specific legislation.
issues.quote: I agree with the authors' assessment that their treatment was ethical in China, but that analysis depended on China's particular legislation that privileged and protected this kind of citizen speech.

issues.text: The general equilibrium analysis is limited to displacement effects among firms and does not consider how firms and bureaucrats would respond once they learn of an external actor selectively boosting posts, which could undermine the policy's long-term effectiveness.
issues.quote: the kind of general equilibrium analysis that the experiment engages in is limited to displacement effects among firms.

issues.text: The external validity limitations are not fully acknowledged in the draft, and the claimed policy impact and cost-effectiveness are asserted rather than demonstrated.
issues.quote: At the same time, there are important limitations to the external validity which are not fully acknowledged in the present draft.
